subject.title: feat(plugin-sdk): generic outbound delivery-report seam; WhatsApp native auto-reply reports provider-accepted sends

question: Should OpenClaw accept openclaw/plugin-sdk/outbound-delivery-report as the public contract for channel self-delivered sends once real WhatsApp/runtime proof is supplied?
rationale: The code path is plausible and fits the extension boundary, but a new public SDK subpath and idempotency contract need maintainer intent before they become a shipped plugin API.

options.title: Accept seam after proof
options.body: Require redacted WhatsApp or runtime hook-observer proof, then land this API shape as the supported channel self-delivery reporting contract.

options.title: Revise API shape first
options.body: Keep the fix direction but rename, narrow, or relocate the SDK surface before contributors and external plugins depend on it.

options.title: Pause into umbrella design
options.body: Leave this PR open or close it in favor of the broader outbound lifecycle-hook contract discussion if maintainers want one canonical observer design first.

recommendation.title: Accept seam after proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted WhatsApp or runtime hook-observer proof, then land this API shape as the supported channel self-delivery reporting contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal spans shared hook mapping, outbound session context, and WhatsApp/plugin boundary refactors.
